quietus.description: Johnny Marr The Age of Everything Former Smiths guitarist settles some scores – with himself, and others When I spoke to Johnny Marr for Huck in 2019, all Morrissey talk was off the table. Marr is a very affable interviewee though, and given that the conversation was going so well, I couldn’t resist slipping in a cheeky question about how an unnamed “certain person” was chipping away at the legacy of The Smiths with his increasingly unhinged pronouncements. “Honestly? I’m not concerned, is the answer,” he replied, generously. “I’m just not. I’m concerned about so many other things in my day and in the living of my life, you know, that that just isn’t one of my concerns. I go out and play...

quietus.description: @ Autosmile Philadelphia duo with an ungoogleable name create dreamy psychedelic worlds with Waterboys flutes adn Beach Boys harmonies Autosmile by @ It’s a great time and a nightmarish time to be an @ (pronounced ‘at’) fan. It’s exciting that the Philadelphia art-folk band’s second album has just been released, but it’s also a faff trying to explain to friends who @ are. Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak are making fresh, entrancing music that communicates places and mindsets in contemporary ways that can’t quite be reduced to any generic label or category. Selfishly, when you listen to the self-proclaimed SEO wet dream’s latest album Autosmile you almost want to keep them to yourself, to…

A prolific improviser, composer and researcher, she is one of the most celebrated figures working in…

quietus.title: Oliver Leith – Doom and the Dooms
quietus.description: Oliver Leith Doom and the Dooms Based on transcriptions direct from tapes found at a jumble sale, the latest from Oliver Leith may be the ideal entry point to the British composer's oeuvre Steady pulse, parallel melodies. Strings undulating with opulent vibrato. Percussive garnish that, clinking and clattering, sounds just like a five-year-old breaking a piggy bank. Endless vacillation between hope and despair. Endless vacillation between stately ceremony and soft frolicking. All processed as if through a stereo-widening plug-in. This is Oliver Leith’s signature style, and it’s easy to start taking it for granted – mostly because of how effortless he makes it sound. Commissioned by Wigmore…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Willis Alan Ramsey :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: More than 50 years after releasing one of the great cult albums of the early ’70s, Willis Alan Ramsey remains an enigma: a singular songwriter whose long-awaited second record has yet to materialize. But as a recent live appearance and a first-ever vinyl reissue of his self-titled debut attest, Ramsey is very much still here — and already thinking beyond the follow-up he once abandoned. We caught up with the Texas songwriter to talk about the making of a classic, the decades since, and the music still to come.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Surprise Chef :: Frogs In A Pond
aquariumdrunkard.description: Like the best giallo scores, Surprise Chef's Frogs In A Pond finds beauty in the uneasy marriage of the sinister and the seductive. Its analog warmth and locked-in grooves evoke a bygone era without becoming trapped in it, blurring the line between recordings from 2026 and 1976. The eerie mood of the compositions, mixed with the 8-track recording, creates an auditory twilight zone that’s both nostalgic and immediate.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Valerie and Her Week of Wonders :: (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
aquariumdrunkard.description: This Halloween when the usual horror soundtrack fare begins to feel a little too familiar, there is Valerie and Her Week of Wonders. Released in 1970, Jaromil Jireš’s surreal Czech fairy tale is a bizarre, beautiful collision of vampires, witchcraft, religious repression, erotic awakening and dream logic. Paired with Luboš Fišer’s score, the whole thing feels like an intermittent phantasmagoria.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Videodrome :: Psycho II (1983)
aquariumdrunkard.description: About midway through Psycho II (1983), you realize you’re not watching a horror sequel, but a carefully constructed character study. Psycho II isn’t really interested in being a sequel or a horror film; it’s interested in the rehabilitation of Norman Bates, and how those in Bates’ orbit react to that. We may have entered the film expecting a boogeyman, but instead we’re watching a fatally flawed hero, and…we’re rooting for him? Yes, we’re actually rooting for Norman Bates.

aquariumdrunkard.title: A La Altura: Visionary Mexican Music 1977-1999
aquariumdrunkard.description: Experimental music history is still, in large part, a Euro-American project. Rare are the efforts that highlight Latin American pioneers like Beatriz Ferreyra or Jocy de Oliveira, and rarer still are histories of electronic scenes with a pop, new age edge. A La Altura: Visionary Mexican Music 1977-1999 excavates the ambient underground of Mexico City, tracing a vibrant, largely overlooked circuit of independent cassette culture, dubbed tapes, and street stalls. Compiled by Carlos Icaza and Mark McNeill after a decade of research into the city’s cassette history, it offers a long-overdue portrait of Mexico’s experimental music underground.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Chris Lyons :: New Love for the Old Flame
aquariumdrunkard.description: After a pair of excellent albums fronting his New Orleans quartet Silver Synthetic, last year's Painters Street saw musician and vocalist Chris Lyons venturing into promising solo pathways. On sophomore record New Love for the Old Flame , Lyons presents a dazzling collection hovering like the forlorn days of the golden AM dial. The comfort of a lazy afternoon personified in sound.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jimmy Webb :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: Jimmy Webb has written some of the great songs in the modern American songbook. After turning 80 in August, he's releasing Yours For The Taking: The Found Songs of Jimmy Webb , via the revived Sun Records. Featuring guests like Michael McDonald, Graham Nash, and Amy Grant, the new album features both new recordings of long lost songs and original demos. With songs that stretch back across the decades, it's a collection that showcases Webb's mastery. He joins us to discuss the magic of a song demo, his upbringing in the church, and his lifelong love of science fiction.

It was the first Nigerian film to be programmed in the official selection at the festival. Variety called Akinola Davies Jr.’s film miraculous. Rotten Tomatoes aggregated the critical assessment as 98% positive. However, there exists a cultural invisibility at home that stands against these genuine international recognitions.
